protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: PASS: Eclipse CNA CVE-2026-1002 is state=PUBLISHED (https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-1002); GHSA-cphf-4846-3xx9 withdrawn_at is null. Vendor issue https://github.com/vert-x3/vertx-web/issues/2836 shows RFC3986.removeDotSegments("bar/../index.html") returning "bar/index.html" instead of a collapsed path, so a request with bar%2F..%2F after the last slash resolves a nonexistent offset, caches the miss in StaticHandlerImpl, and later legitimate GETs return HTTP 404. The core defect is RFC 3986 §5.2.4 rule C: lastIndexOf("/") then delete only if pos != -1 leaves a slash-free output segment. 4.x fix d007e7b418543eb1567fe95cf20f5450a5c2d047 and 5.x fix 5b67f5d17788b2483d277c760f3f8154f9b2fed0 both replace those guards with obuf.setLength(pos == -1 ? 0 : pos).

findings: CVE-2026-1002/GHSA-cphf-4846-3xx9 is a real availability bug: RFC 3986 rule C in Vert.x Core path normalization fails when the output buffer has no slash, enabling encoded bar%2F..%2F requests to poison Vert.x Web StaticHandler negative cache.

Smallest surviving public first-write of the vulnerable pos != -1/delete branches is d5f646b101377ed2a842dfef00139b509b3bbd71; parent 5a79bf707794078a842800be5ba862a218e64c6c lacks removeDots entirely.
e75a0a15aea7a575ebf865b3ed0839dfd4c3e52c is a 2024 move/copy of the already-flawed algorithm into RFC3986.removeDotSegments, not a new causal implementation.
Direct fixes are d007e7b418543eb1567fe95cf20f5450a5c2d047 (4.5.24) and 5b67f5d17788b2483d277c760f3f8154f9b2fed0 (5.0.7); tag ancestry matches the CNA/GHSA patched boundaries.
BIC authorship is human Julien Viet with no AI/bot/generator marker, so primary_verdict NOT_AI stands.
